title: A Galaxy That Makes Neutrinos Without a Black Hole
hook: Astronomers expected a feeding black hole behind a flood of cosmic neutrinos. Instead they found furious star formation — hinting dusty starburst galaxies seed the high-energy neutrino sky.
key_points: Space is awash in high-energy neutrinos, but pinning down their sources is hard.
Supermassive black holes feeding on gas were the leading suspected source.
A dusty galaxy nicknamed 'Shadow Blaster' appears to make neutrinos via extreme star formation.
Hidden starburst galaxies could account for a significant share of cosmic high-energy neutrinos.
Neutrinos barely interact with matter, so they escape thick dust that traps light.
content_html: Space is filled with high-energy neutrinos — ghostly particles that stream through almost everything untouched. Tracing where they come from is one of astronomy's hardest puzzles, and the usual prime suspect is gas swirling into a supermassive black hole. A galaxy nicknamed "Shadow Blaster" points to another culprit.
extra_html: Researchers found that this distant, dust-shrouded galaxy may be churning out neutrinos through extreme star formation rather than a feeding black hole. Bursts of newborn stars — and the violent supernovae they leave behind — can turn a galaxy into a natural particle accelerator. Because neutrinos barely interact with matter, they slip out of even thick dust that traps light, carrying information from deep inside. If many such hidden "starburst" galaxies behave this way, they could supply a significant fraction of the universe's high-energy neutrinos — reshaping where we think this cosmic particle flux is born. See the full release for details.

related.hook: When a giant star dies, its core collapses and its outer layers blast away in a supernova that can briefly outshine an entire galaxy — leaving behind something extraordinary.

related.hook: One of the most energetic cosmic rays ever caught hit Earth with the energy of a thrown brick — packed into a single particle. New work says it may be a heavy nucleus, not a proton.

related.title: JUNO's First Look at Shape-Shifting Neutrinos
related.hook: A giant detector buried under China caught neutrinos changing identity mid-flight — and in just 59 days made one of the sharpest measurements yet of the ghost particle's habits.

flashcards.prompt: What surprising source of cosmic neutrinos did the 'Shadow Blaster' galaxy point to?

choices.text: Extreme star formation, not a feeding supermassive black hole
A supermassive black hole swallowing a passing star
A collision between two neutron stars

flashcards.explanation_html: The dusty galaxy appears to produce high-energy neutrinos through intense star formation rather than the usually-suspected supermassive black hole.

flashcards.prompt: Why can neutrinos reveal what's happening deep inside a dust-shrouded galaxy?
flashcards.back_html: Neutrinos barely interact with matter, so they slip out of thick dust that blocks light — carrying information straight from the galaxy's hidden interior.

flashcards.prompt: If many hidden starburst galaxies make neutrinos this way, what would it imply?

choices.text: They could supply a significant fraction of the universe's high-energy neutrinos
Supermassive black holes produce no neutrinos at all
Cosmic neutrinos must all come from within our own galaxy

flashcards.explanation_html: The discovery suggests dust-filled starburst galaxies could account for a sizeable share of cosmic high-energy neutrinos, broadening where we think they originate.
